title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes
content:
Quick scratch notes for partnership outreach + account research. Most of this is stream-of-consciousness, will refine into a one-pager and outreach sequence.

Account: Acme Cloud Services (target: partnerships / integrations)
- HQ: SF, cloud infra + managed services for midmarket and enterprise.
- Funding: Series D, ~2024 growth; recently announced multi-region expansion in EU.
- Key execs: CTO = Priya Raman (strong infra background), Head of Ecosystem = Ben Torres (runs partner programs).
- Recent news: announced managed database product + compliance push (SOC2 + EU residency). Likely priorities: predictable costs, latency SLAs for AI features, compliance for customers.

Why Redwood might matter to them:
- Use case: adding LLM features to product (customer support, in-app assistants) without managing GPU ops.
- Sell: predictable latency + routing (multi-region), private deployment option for regulated customers, cost controls via Optimize (batching/quantization suggestions).
- Competitive angle: they may have evaluated large cloud endpoints; Redwood differentiator = unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private + cost/latency telemetry (helps SREs & product).

Signals from public sources / notes:
- Job postings for "AI infrastructure engineer" and "platform partnerships" -> budget/interest in AI features.
- Blog post about EU expansion mentions need for data residency for banking customers -> private deployments + KMS integration is a direct hook.
- Investors/board emphasize margins & predictable infra costs -> cost reduction story resonates.

Potential stakeholders to target:
- Ben Torres (Head of Ecosystem) — partnership lead, influencers for integrations programs.
- Priya Raman (CTO) — technical champion for any private/dedicated deployment.
- Dir of Product (AI/Platform) — cares about dev UX and rollout risk.
- SRE/Platform leads — care about quotas, latency, observability.

Outbound subject lines (A/B test):
- "Reduce LLM infra spend while keeping latencies predictable"
- "Private inference option for EU residency & SOC2 customers"
- "Pilot: Dedicated GPU capacity + cost telemetry for Acme Cloud"

Cold email draft (short):
Hi Ben / Priya —
I’m Aisha at Redwood Inference. We help engineering teams run LLM inference with predictable latency, cost, and private deployment options. Given Acme’s EU residency push and managed DB product, we’d love to explore a short pilot: dedicated capacity + workload-aware batching to reduce per-token cost while preserving SLOs.
Are you available for 20 minutes next week to discuss a small pilot?
Thanks,
Aisha

Cold email draft (longer, technical):
Hey Ben —
Saw Acme’s post about EU expansion and platformized DB offering — congrats. At Redwood we work with infra (and product) teams to standardize LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and VPC/on-prem modes. Typical wins: 30–50% cost reduction from batching/kv-cache + consistent 95th-percentile latency for interactive assistants. We can also provide private control plane + KMS for EU-residency customers.
If it’s of interest, can we set a 20-min sync to map requirements and propose a 6-week pilot?
Aisha Patel

Call script bullets (discovery -> close):
- Intro: quick 30s why Redwood (prod-first inference, private option, cost controls).
- Discovery questions:
  - What LLM features are in roadmap? (assistants, summarization, search, embeddings)
  - Expected QPS and latency targets? 95th/99th percentiles?
  - Data residency / compliance needs? KMS/HSM requirements?
  - Do you prefer managed endpoints or customer-managed infra?
  - Current infra pain: cost spikes, cache misses, model versioning, unreliable throughput?
- Value props to highlight based on answers:
  - If compliance/residency: private deployment, KMS integration, audit logs.
  - If cost focus: Optimize toolkit + batching & caching recommendations, model quantization options.
  - If reliability: smart routing, auto-fallback, SLA-backed dedicated pools.
- Next steps ask: propose a small pilot (4–6 weeks) with defined success metrics (p95 latency < X ms, cost reduction >= Y%).

Common objections + rebuttals (quick lines):
- "We already use [cloud vendor endpoint]" -> "Totally — Redwood can sit in front of existing endpoints or replace them depending on needs; customers often adopt us because of predictable cost and unified control across environments."
- "Not ready to move sensitive workloads" -> "We offer private deployments (VPC / on-prem) with KMS/HSM support and audit logging — we can run a pilot in a customer-isolated environment."
- "How do we measure cost savings?" -> "We run a discovery baseline of token throughput + latency, then simulate batching/kv-cache and estimate savings; pilot includes telemetry at token/request level so you can see unit economics."
- "Integration work looks heavy" -> "We provide SDKs + reference integrations and partner with platform teams for a one-week integration sprint for common flows (chat, embeddings)."

Pilot scope suggestion (minimal viable pilot):
- Duration: 4–6 weeks
- Objectives: validate p95 latencies, measure per-token cost delta, verify model compatibility + KMS flows for EU-residency.
- Deliverables: runbook for integration, per-route dashboards, cost/latency baseline vs pilot, rollback plan.

Notes for internal follow-up:
- Ask Solutions Eng for a rough T-shirt estimate for 4-week integration + 1 engineer half-time. (Marco?)
- Product: confirm whether we have a prebuilt KMS flow for Acme's provider (Azure Wales? check). (Sophie?)
- Legal: flag potential data residency / DPA items early.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm Ben Torres' correct email (LinkedIn vs company site mismatch).
- Get list of prioritized product use-cases (support bot, in-app assistant, search) before pilot scoping.
- Draft one-pager + 2-slide tech summary for Ben/Priya (value props + pilot plan).

Rough timeline:
- This week: verify contacts + send intro.
- Week 1–2: discovery, baseline telemetry collection.
- Week 3–4: pilot deploy + compare metrics.
- Week 5: review + scale decision.

Misc scratch lines (drop-in ideas):
- Could propose a co-marketing blog if pilot goes well (mutual PR).
- Consider offering an onboarding credit for pilot to lower friction (tied to MSA).

-- end of scratch notes --
